ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–80 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct yellow-to-orange nuchal collar and dark, vertical bars on the neck. It features keeled scales and a dark subocular streak.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Fowlea schnurrenbergeri* by the distinct, narrow black vertical bars on its neck, which are more sharply defined than the broader, irregular blotches of *F. piscator*.
ai.habitat: The Bar-necked Keelback inhabits moist, low-to-mid-elevation areas, typically frequenting streams, marshes, and rice paddies within dense tropical forest environments.
ai.behavior: The Bar-necked Keelback is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for amphibians like frogs and toads in and around water bodies throughout its range.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Fowlea schnurrenbergeri* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Fowlea schnurrenbergeri* is endemic to the Gangetic plains of northern India, specifically recorded in the states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar at low elevations.
